hint.text: Commas are used to separate two main clauses. There should be a comma placed before the coordinating conjunction that joins two main clauses together.

instruction.text: Use the coordinating conjunction to join the two sentences together.

atoms.a:
I used to have a cat. He ran away.

but
atoms.sound: I used to have a cat. He ran away.

atoms.a:
I saved some money. I can go on a holiday.

so
atoms.sound: I saved some money. I can go on a holiday.

atoms.a:
Lara painted the kitchen. Ben painted the bathroom.

and
atoms.sound: Lara painted the kitchen. Ben painted the bathroom.

atoms.a:
We could go to the beach. We could go to the park.

or
atoms.sound: We could go to the beach. We could go to the park.
She didn’t answer my call, nor did she reply to my messages
b: ++She didn’t answer my call, nor did she reply to my messages.
She didn’t answer my call nor, did she reply to my messages.

atoms.sound: I ran as fast as possible, yet I did not win.
b: ++I ran as fast as possible, yet I did not win.
I ran as fast as possible yet, I did not win.

atoms.sound: We went inside, and it started to rain.
b: ++We went inside, and it started to rain.
We went inside and, it started to rain.
